purpose: Define in advance when legacy SWAP secondary surface-water ownership may be retired in an external-Ribasim application, without confusing that decision with full legacy feature parity.

COUPLED_STATE_OWNERSHIP_RETIREMENT.claim: For a declared SWAP5+Ribasim application profile, SWAP no longer owns the represented secondary surface-water storage/level/control realization.
required: Q1A external Ribasim state/discharge ownership passes with direct mass ledger for the declared fixed-weir representation.
Q1B or equivalent external supply realization passes when supply is in scope.
Q2A passes if soil-state-driven automatic target policy is in scope.
Q2B realization passes if automatic target realization is in scope.
Q3A signed lower exchange and availability transaction passes when reverse exchange is in scope.
Q3B passes for runoff/rapid/top-surface exchange classes that are active in the declared profile.
Mode gate enforces exactly one physical surface-water state owner.
Every active exchange is booked exactly once per model with opposite signs.
No legacy SWST/WLS availability limiter remains hidden in SWAP when Ribasim owns storage.
may_exclude_by_application_contract: nonlinear SWQHR1 parity if the coupled application profile does not use it
SWQHR2 legacy threshold seam if not used

FULL_LEGACY_FUNCTIONAL_PARITY.claim: Every scientifically retained legacy surface-water-management behaviour has an explicit equivalent or documented intentional change.
required_additionally: Q1C nonlinear SWQHR1 representation or explicit exact alternative
FULL_LEGACY_FUNCTIONAL_PARITY.note: This stronger claim is not required merely to operate a narrower Ribasim-coupled production profile.

WHOLE_FILE_DELETION.claim: No remaining compiled production responsibility requires the legacy surfacewater.f90 container.
required_additionally: all retained SWAP exchange physics has a non-legacy production owner
all required adapters/configuration are typed outside the legacy container
no active standalone SWAP5 profile depends on deleting the same modern capability
source/dependency and preservation gates prove removal does not delete qualified standalone F-CI52 functionality
WHOLE_FILE_DELETION.note: Whole-file deletion is a code-migration decision distinct from external-owner architecture.

fail_closed_rules: A coupled application cannot activate internal SWAP surface-water storage and external Ribasim ownership for the same physical store.
An open feature parity item cannot be silently treated as equivalent; it must be qualified or excluded explicitly by the application contract.
A Ribasim capacity/availability reduction cannot be applied only after SWAP has committed the unconstrained transfer.
A passing mass balance does not by itself prove correct ownership or correct process semantics.
current_expected_outcome: Evidence is trending toward coupled-state-ownership retirement being supportable for a bounded Ribasim profile while full legacy parity and whole-file deletion remain separate stronger decisions.
